Title: Call of the Great Beast and self-contest

Messages.Author: Ashenbach
Messages.Body:
Hello,

Let's say i have a Nergal in play with a Discipline card on him, making a 11 cap vampire and a vampire named "Call the Great Beast" in play (previously put in play by another Baali).

¿Can Nergal play another Call the Great Beast action? ¿What happens if he can?

Thanks in advance.

Regards.

Messages.Author: mipopo3
Messages.Body:
"¿Can Nergal play another Call the Great Beast action?"
Yes
"¿What happens if he can?"
It is burned once it resolves.

Warning: Spoiler!

DECK CONSTRUCTION

CAUTION: Be careful about putting duplicates of the same unique cards in your deck. You cannot control more than one of the same unique card at a time, and you cannot voluntarily contest cards with yourself (if some effect would force you to contest a card with yourself, then you simply burn the incoming copy of the unique card). On the other hand, you may wish to have a second copy handy in case the first is burned.

Messages.Author: mipopo3
Messages.Body:
This need to be reflected in the current rulebook.
Thus amended text from:
"You cannot control more than one of the same unique card at a time, and you cannot voluntarily contest cards with yourself (if some effect would force you to contest a card with yourself, then you simply burn the incoming copy of the unique card)."

Needs to be:
"You cannot control more than one of the same unique card at a time, and you cannot voluntarily play a card that would trigger a contest with yourself (if some effect would force you to contest a card with yourself, then you simply burn the incoming copy of the unique card)."

as this covers all similar situations including trying to play "The, Coven" form your hand, while you have "The, Coven" that is from other player in your control,*edit* Summoning History on minor, the, Summoning, Split the Veil, ... that will put an unique ally in play that is in your control already *edit*

As 11 cap Baali with Call the Great Beast (that is a vampire) on the field cant play a card that would trigger a contest scenario.

OR

We can clearly see that the issue comes from card not being unique, and that triggers effect constitutes vampire recruitment: "action to bring a vampire in to play", witch is not defined in the card text, thus it needs to be updated. If we are to rely on the old ruling.

Warning: Spoiler!

+1 stealth action. Recruitment
Put this card with X ritual counters on this Baali, where X is this Baali's capacity. This Baali can put 1 ritual counter on this card as a +1 stealth action. If this card has 11 or more ritual counters, move this card to your ready region, burn this Baali and choose three Disciplines; this card becomes a 9-capacity unique clanless Independent infernal vampire with 4 strength, 3 bleed, the chosen three Disciplines at the superior level and 9 blood who can enter combat with a minion as a Ⓓ action and can prevent 1 damage each combat.

This would apply to Summoning History superior, Creation Rites, The, Embrace, Third Tradition: Progeny, ...

Thus we are back at this topic, so rule change or text change.

I will not point out that the current rulebook is the same as in 94, and it was not corrected at any point from then to today.

Regarding the use of The, Summoning, and other cards, I was referring to the recruitment of a copy of a unique ally, if I must quote myself:
"That will put an unique ally in play that is in your control already"
As the flow goes, I play the summoning, find a copy, and that is the only ally I find; thus, it (the ally) can't be played. This would fail The Summoning like there was no ally in the deck.

Thus, a clear change in the rulebook covers that case.

Regarding wording "action to bring a vampire in to play", I would like to call BS on this, as I have not seen this used in any card text (excluding Summoning History) and the rulebook in any shape or form, thus making this ruling from 2010 moot in today's game.

There is no added ruling on Hatchling, Embrace, Becoming, ... to refer to this "action to bring a vampire in to play", not sure how it came to be, was there some new ruling in the works, but for now, let's put it under the old ruling, and do what we can, and update the rulebook to cover the case better, so any new player can refer to the rulebook.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
Its morning and theres a wall of text to read. I didnt read it all, but I generally agree with Mipopo3 here. The action card "call the great beast" is not unique. There is no logical reason why you shouldn't be able to perform call the great beast action as per game rules. The "You cannot attempt what you cannot do" does not qualify here because you can actually do the action. The action is not an action to put a vampire directly into play, but instead it would do it in the form of a delayed trigger. This shouldn't count as an action to put a vampire into play. The trigger is completely separate.

Also, the way I would interpret this (obviously Im not a judge), is that you could perform the action even if it resulted in 11 counters on the card, but call the great beast simply couldn't transform into Great beast, because its unique and there is already one in play. The card would just sit there with the counters until it would no longer contest. That's how I would do it in a way that also satisfied all the rules.

ps. for simplicity, the card should read "This card becomes... named great beast". That it would change its name would further implicate that the action and the vampire are two separate things.

Smoking craters tell no tales.
—Tex talks Battletech

That much is obvious, allow me try to spell it out for you as much as I'm able given the limited time.

You are methusaleh A at 15 pool, your only vampire in play is 11 cap anarch Call the Great Beast who has chosen superior Presence, Temporis and Quietus. They have five blood on them. In addition your prey Methusaleh B has played Barrenness at Maleficia level on your controlled Call the Great Beast, they have no minions in play and are at 25 pool. You have played four master disciplines on your controlled Call the Great Beast, they are 2 Obfuscate, 2 Dementation. In your uncontrolled region is vampire banished by methuselah C.That vampire is Call the Great beast with superior presence, temporis and quietus chosen but without the disciplines played on them and they have 8 blood on them. Your crypt is empty as all the other vampires you had have been Graverobbed across the table to methuselah D who has then played The Name Forgotten equally on them and used one to diablerize another resulting in your crypt becoming empty. In your ash heap you have 4 Call the Great Beasts and other cards there have been burned away by Trochomancy by your predator methuselah E who has attempted to bleed you but can no longer do that due to having no minions.

1) You have Summon history in your hand, you decide to play it at superior at 0 blood, what happens? You complete the action successfully and search for 0 capacity vampire but as there is no targets you can find, you can not put vampire to play.

2) You have Undue Influence in your hand, you decide to play it at quietus, what happens?
You are trying to put vampire into play with sterile vampire. Despite your arguments how Sterile is just a word on Barrenness and it does not say anything about not being able to put vampire into play judge rules you are cheating as you have been in argument over it at VEKN forum, clearly know the rules and are deliberately mispotraying the rules, you get 163. Cheating - Fraud and disqualification without Prize as there should be zero tolerance for this type of activity.

3) You have Call the Great Beast at hand, you decide to play it, what happens?
You are trying to put vampire into play that self contests. Despite your arguments how you are not putting vampire into play judge rules you are cheating as you have been in argument over it at VEKN forum, clearly know the rules and are deliberately mispotraying the rules, you get 163. Cheating - Fraud and disqualification without Prize as there should be zero tolerance for this type of activity.

4) You have Undue Influence in your hand, you decide to play it at presence, what happens? You bleed successfully and add 1 blood to the chosen vampire.

Compare the end results and you might see how they are not similar and in fact different. You can also see why it's important that rules questions are not left with what if or mayhaps answers as their consequences to new players during tournament play might be quite harsh, hence Ankha has not changed their first reply to the question and if there is a change, it will be clearly marked and announced.

Feel free to ponder the difference of the above scenario if there was no Barrenness on your vampire and if the vampire in your uncontrolled region was instead Annazir at 8 blood that escaped the Name Forgotten due to being only copy you own.
How would Undue Influence work at quietus?
How would Call the Great Beast?

Notice the difference and what is the limiting factor. Now take the discipline cards away but change the Banished vampire back to Call the Great Beast at 8 blood.
How would Undue Influence work at quietus?
How would Call the Great Beast when the calling vampire is at 9 capacity?
Notice what actions put vampires into play, when and how.

Please read this reply carefully, use proxy cards to play it out if you have hard time following what is happening in the example. Read the card texts, as there are multiples I have put them behind spoiler this time, they are paramount to understanding this. Do not attempt to shorten them, change their locations or invent your own layouts while going through the scenario outlines as this is not suggestions thread, but a rules question thread that deals with the game as it is now.
